candidates.title: Run repeatable tests against proprietary assistants

demandEvidence.chore: Teams need to iterate on proprietary assistants by running repeatable tests against them.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: help teams iterate against proprietary assistants like Muse and Instinct.

ease.reason: A student can compare fixed prompts and expected outcomes manually, but the post supplies no implementation steps or testing capability reference.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: teams adapting proprietary assistants may pay for repeatable checks; this Show HN statement proves no buyers or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test harness for a small set of operator-provided prompts is plausible, but assistant access and judging accuracy are unverified.

autonomy.reason: A fixed test set could rerun and flag changed answers; a person must judge results, and no automation mechanics are documented.

evidence.reason: The post directly says the tool helps teams iterate against proprietary assistants, but gives no workflow detail or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the stated need supports a small test-set experiment, but implementation support and demonstrated customer demand are absent.

candidates.title: Trigger SMTP email from another app

demandEvidence.chore: Configure an automation to send an email through DigitalAka when another app triggers it.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want a Make scenario to send an email through DigitalAka when a trigger occurs in another app.

ease.reason: A student can model a trigger and draft an SMTP request, but the discussion does not document a working connection or supplied implementation reference.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small service firms may pay for reliable app-triggered email setup; the request establishes no customer payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can accept a test trigger and prepare a message, while SMTP credentials, provider compatibility and delivery need testing.

autonomy.reason: A trigger-to-message loop is bounded, but no connection mechanics are evidenced and a person should approve test messages before delivery.

evidence.reason: The request names Make, DigitalAka, email and an app trigger, but gives no setup detail, frequency or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the request is concrete enough for a mock trigger-to-email experiment, but the supplied evidence does not document implementation capability.

rejected.title: A Mac menu bar app that brings the Dock to the pointer
rejected.reason: The assigned post is only a product title; it states no concrete customer chore or request from which to derive demand evidence.

rejected.title: A Pinterest publishing node for n8n
rejected.reason: The post lists capabilities of an already built node, including schedules and batch publishing, but does not state a concrete unmet chore or request; treating its feature list as customer demand would overread the evidence.

rejected.title: Autonomous lead qualification and CRM enrichment
rejected.reason: The assigned post says an end-to-end workflow was built; it does not state a concrete existing chore, request, or buyer need.

rejected.title: Fixing an empty recipient field in drafted emails
rejected.reason: The excerpt describes one configuration error in a particular draft, not a recurring service chore; automating this isolated bug would invent broader demand.

rejected.title: Cloudflare R2 signer configuration
rejected.reason: The assigned source asks one technical configuration question about a 403 error. It is an isolated support issue, not a supported repeatable business chore for a proposed AI service.

steps.message: Assessed all seven sealed discussion identities. Two concrete tasks received five-criterion experiments but remain below threshold without implementation evidence; five were excluded for lacking supported repeatable demand or describing an isolated technical issue. No post proposed.
